doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Birdland, Wayne Shorter and Curtis Fuller, and Raph's blues solo
summary: Raph says he soloed little but tells of playing opposite Blakey and Dizzy at Birdland. He mentions Wayne Shorter's arrangement for Mulligan and a blues solo praised by Curtis Fuller.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Were you called upon to do much improvising and soloing?

Not a lot. There are two or three records that are floating around that I have a little bit of improvisation on. I did — playing with Mulligan’s band at Birdland, we played opposite Dizzy Gillespie, we played opposite Art Blakey, we played opposite many very good jazz

bands. As a matter of fact it’s funny, I went to school with Wayne Shorter. We both went to NYU. He was a half a year behind me. And I’m playing here with Gerry Mulligan and Wayne is playing with Art Blakey. In fact I got Wayne to write an arrangement for Mulligan’s big band which he did and Gerry played, a thing called “Mama G” is one of the tunes that Gerry played with the band. But along with Wayne was Freddie Hubbard and also Curtis Fuller. And Curtis I loved. I just did an album of his called “Cabin in the Sky” right around that time when we did that particular Birdland job. And I had Brookmeyer and Willie Dennis there in the Mulligan band and Curtis walking around listening to the band. And I had the nerve to stand up and play a blues solo on one of the tunes that Gerry had, because Gerry finally — sometimes he wouldn’t show up until the first couple of tunes and the band would just play something and we’d share the solos. So I would stand up occasionally and play. And I remember at one point I stood up and played this blues thing. And I thought oh my God this is horrible but I have to get through the 24 bars or whatever it is. And after it was over, after the set was over, Curtis came over and he says “hey man that was very nice.” I thought oh my God. I’m in heaven. You didn’t have to say that to me. So I can play but it’s like you wear a sailor’s hat and to your mother and father you’re a sailor but to a sailor you’re not a sailor. You know what I mean? I can play jazz. To a jazz player I’m not a jazz player.
